question.text: How many of Europe's top 20 grocery retailers will have public shrimp welfare commitments before July 2027?
question.resolution_criteria:
This question will resolve as the number of the following retailers that, before July 1, 2027, have announced and not retracted any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments, according to [credible sources](https://www.metaculus.com/faq/#definitions) such as the Shrimp Welfare Project's [Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps):

* Ahold Delhaize
* Aldi
* Asda
* Auchan
* Carrefour
* Co-op
* E. Leclerc
* Edeka-Gruppe
* Intermarché
* J. Sainsbury's
* Jerónimo Martins
* Magnit
* Mercadona
* Metro AG
* Migros
* Rewe Group
* Schwarz Group
* Systeme U
* Tesco
* X5 Retail Group
question.fine_print:
A welfare commitment must have been announced at any point before July 1, 2027, including before this question opens, but need not have been implemented.   

In case of grocery retailer mergers, entities are still treated distinctly for purposes of this question. Thus, if two companies in the above list merge and the successor entity has a qualifying policy, then both slots count toward the 10 that are needed for a **Yes** resolution.

research:
# Shrimp welfare commitments among Europe's top 20 grocery retailers: research notes (as of 2026-11-05)

On my reading, 13 of the 20 listed retailers already have a public shrimp welfare commitment. Retailers that are subsidiaries or operate under a group name are mapped to the listed names: Albert Heijn counts for Ahold Delhaize, Les Mousquetaires for Intermarché, Lidl for Schwarz Group. The SWP page alone supports only 6. The question's background text mentions a threshold of 10 for "Yes", which doesn't fit a numeric question.

## 1. Resolution source
- 2026-02-16 (last update): SWP's "Where Can I Purchase Humanely Farmed Shrimps?" page lists 12 retailers with both stunning and no-ablation commitments. 6 of them are on the question's list: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Asda, Albert Heijn (Ahold Delhaize) and Les Mousquetaires (Intermarché). It gives no dates for individual commitments and has not been updated since the Lidl, Aldi, Auchan and U pledges. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)
- The resolution wording counts "any shrimp or prawn welfare commitments" from credible sources, so ablation-only or partial pledges probably count.

## 2. Current status: nearly settled
Commitments I found, 13 in total:
- **Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Asda:** listed by SWP. Asda pledged to end ablation by 2027 and switch to electrical stunning by 2028 (Feb 2026). [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/02/12/uks-asda-commits-to-ban-shrimp-eyestalk-ablation-ice-slurry-stunning/)
- **Ahold Delhaize:** Albert Heijn's target was no ablation and stunning for all own-brand tropical shrimp by 2025. [AH](https://over.ah.nl/overzicht/vis-schelp-en-schaaldieren)
- **Intermarché, Auchan, Système U, Carrefour, Aldi:** Mousquetaires and Auchan ended ablation in January 2026 and target stunning by 2030. U targets no ablation by end-2027 and stunning by 2030. Carrefour targets no ablation by 2029, with no stunning pledge. Aldi (France) targets 2031 for ablation and 2035 for stunning. [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- **Aldi Süd:** global policy (April 2026): no ablation by 2030, electrical stunning by 2035. **Aldi Nord:** no ablation by 2029 for whiteleg shrimp and by 2031 for giant shrimp. [SeafoodSource](https://www.seafoodsource.com/news/foodservice-retail/with-aldi-s-d-commitment-all-major-uk-supermarkets-have-set-time-bound-shrimp-welfare-standards), [Lebensmittel Praxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-aktuell/46113-lebensmittelhandel-schwere-garnelenzucht-vorwuerfe-gegen-aldi.html)
- **Schwarz Group (Lidl):** ablation removed from 100% of its international permanent own-label farmed shrimp since January 2026. No stunning date at group level, but Lidl GB pledged electrical stunning by end-2026. [Lidl](https://info.lidl/en/our-responsibility/acting-fairly/fish-seafood), [GSA](https://www.globalseafood.org/advocate/lidl-gb-bans-eyestalk-ablation-for-farmed-prawns-joining-nine-other-u-k-retailers/)
- **Metro AG:** 2025-11-25: mechanical or electrical stunning required for all own-brand crustaceans. Shrimp suppliers are asked, not required, to avoid ablation. No timelines given. [The Fish Site](https://thefishsite.com/articles/metro-introduces-new-stunning-requirements-for-seafood-supply-chain)
- **Rewe:** 2025-10-12: aims for ablation-free own-brand supply chains "by 2027 at the latest", with conventional shrimp allowed until 2030. This is a softer, spokesperson-level statement and may not count. [watson](https://www.watson.de/leben/supermarkt/309791620-supermarkt-garnelen-grausam-gezuechtet-deutsche-maerkte-unter-druck)

No commitment found, 7 in total:
- **E. Leclerc:** reported as refusing to commit (Oct 2026). [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234362)
- **Edeka:** gave no comment and was cited as having no timeline.
- **Jerónimo Martins, Magnit, Mercadona, Migros, X5:** I searched and found nothing.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir reports on the ICAW findings for French retailers. [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-10-19: Economie Matin reports Leclerc refusing to commit. ICAW says 50% of the French market lacks a full commitment. [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234362)
- 2026-10-16/18: ICAW publishes its French report "Souffrance en Rayon", and AFP covers the campaign. [Sud Radio](https://www.sudradio.fr/societe/la-grande-distribution-appelee-a-sengager-contre-la-maltraitance-des-crevettes-delevage)
- 2026-04-09: Aldi Süd makes its global shrimp pledge, meaning all 11 major UK supermarkets now have time-bound commitments. [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/04/09/aldi-sud-joins-other-major-uk-supermarkets-with-shrimp-stunning-commitment/)
- 2026-02-12: Asda commitment. [Undercurrent](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/02/12/uks-asda-commits-to-ban-shrimp-eyestalk-ablation-ice-slurry-stunning/)
- 2025-11-25: Metro policy. [The Fish Site](https://thefishsite.com/articles/metro-introduces-new-stunning-requirements-for-seafood-supply-chain)

## 4. Base rates
- Tesco was the first major pledge, in 2024. By February 2026, SWP counted 6 of the 20 listed retailers. By November 2026, press reports cover about 13. That is roughly 7 new retailers in about 9 months, mostly in the UK, France and Germany, driven by ICAW and SWP campaigns.
- I found no commitment that was retracted. Certification schemes are also tightening: ASC plans to end ablation by 2029-2031 and BAP by 2030. That makes ablation pledges easier to adopt. [Lidl](https://info.lidl/en/our-responsibility/acting-fairly/fish-seafood)

## 5. Other forecasts
- None of the supplied Kalshi or Polymarket markets match this question. They cover beef prices, NYC grocery stores and similar topics.
- I couldn't find the Metaculus community forecast for this question, and no other expert forecast turned up.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- ICAW's campaign targeting Leclerc and its push on German retailers (Edeka, Rewe and Lidl stunning) is ongoing. Biocoop says it is working on new commitments for 2027; it isn't on the list.
- SWP may update its page, which so far counts only 6 of the listed retailers.
- Rewe's 2027 own-brand ablation deadline falls before resolution.
- Political pressure: the Dutch House of Representatives has moved to end eyestalk ablation. [Hatchery FM](https://hatcheryfm.com/shrimp/the-dutch-house-of-representatives-aims-to-end-eyestalk-ablation-in-shrimp)
- Main resolution risks:
  - **Strictness:** whether Metro's "request", Rewe's "aim" and the Carrefour or Lidl pledges without stunning count.
  - **Retailer mapping:** whether pledges by national subsidiaries count for the group (Lidl GB for Schwarz, Aldi Nord/Süd for "Aldi", Albert Heijn for Ahold Delhaize).
  - **Unchecked retailers:** I didn't find anything for Migros, Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit or X5, so a small chance of a missed policy remains.

## 1. Resolution source

A February 2026 graphic on the page is an image I could not read. [SWP](https://www.shrimpwelfareproject.org/blog/where-can-i-purchase-humanely-farmed-shrimps)
- The page looks out of date: it does not include the 2026 commitments from Aldi, Lidl, Auchan, Système U or Carrefour described below.

## 2. Current status
Based on credible press reports, the count appears to be **11 retailers**: Ahold Delhaize (via Albert Heijn), Aldi, Asda, Auchan, Carrefour, Co-op, Intermarché, Sainsbury's, Schwarz (via Lidl), Système U and Tesco. If the old binary threshold of 10 in the fine print were applied, it would already be met. Points of interpretation:
- Ahold Delhaize counts only through Albert Heijn. I found no group-wide or Delhaize policy.
- Schwarz counts through Lidl. Lidl GB has a stunning commitment and its core own-brand range is ablation-free. Lidl France has dropped ablation but made no stunning commitment, and I found nothing for Lidl Germany or Kaufland.
- Carrefour's stunning promise is reported inconsistently, but its ablation commitment is clear. I could not find a primary Carrefour document.
- "Co-op" presumably means the UK Co-op, as on the SWP list.
- I found no commitment from E. Leclerc (it declined to comment), Edeka, Rewe, Mercadona, Migros, Metro, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit or X5. Rewe is mentioned only in critical NGO reporting.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- 2026-11-03: Que Choisir, reporting on the ICAW report, says:
  - Auchan and Mousquetaires stopped ablation for own-brand shrimp in January 2026 and target stunning by 2030.
  - Système U will end ablation by the end of 2027 and adopt stunning by 2030.
  - Aldi will end ablation by 2031 and adopt stunning by 2035.
  - Carrefour will end ablation by 2029.
  - Lidl and Casino dropped ablation in 2026.
  - Leclerc has no commitment.
  [Que Choisir](https://www.quechoisir.org/actualite-crevettes-d-elevage-des-pratiques-cruelles-des-engagements-inegaux-n179190/)
- 2026-10-19: Economie Matin says Intermarché, U and Auchan target 2030 for both measures across all ranges, and Aldi targets 2035. Carrefour will ban ablation by 2027-2029 and promises stunning "à partir de 2027". Leclerc has made no commitments. [Economie Matin](https://www.economiematin.fr/?p=234362)
- 2026-10-16: ICAW published its report "Souffrance en Rayon". It says 50% of the French market is still covered by retailers with no or only partial commitments as of 2026-10-01. [AFP via Figaro](https://figaronautisme.meteoconsult.fr/actus-nautisme-flash/2026-10-18/93243-la-grande-distribution-appelee-a-s-engager-contre-la-maltraitance-des-crevettes-d-elevage), [Consoglobe](https://www.consoglobe.com/crevettes-elevage-souffrance-animale-supermarches-cg)
- 2026-04-09: Aldi Süd announced a global policy: no ablation by 2030 and electrical stunning by 2035, covering Europe, the US and Australia. All 11 major UK supermarkets now have shrimp welfare targets. Lidl has committed to stunning in Great Britain only. [Global Seafood Alliance](https://www.globalseafood.org/?p=70837)
- Date not confirmed: Aldi Nord will phase out ablation by 2029 for whiteleg shrimp and by 2031 for giant tiger prawns. [Lebensmittel Praxis](https://lebensmittelpraxis.de/handel-aktuell/46113-lebensmittelhandel-schwere-garnelenzucht-vorwuerfe-gegen-aldi.html)
- 2026-02-12: Asda committed to ending ablation by 2027 and electrical stunning by 2028. [Undercurrent News](https://www.undercurrentnews.com/2026/02/12/uks-asda-commits-to-ban-shrimp-eyestalk-ablation-ice-slurry-stunning/)
- ICAW is campaigning against Lidl in Germany and Switzerland. [Presseportal](https://www.presseportal.ch/de/pm/100103541/100940964)

## 4. Base rates
- 2024: Tesco banned ablation, the first of the 20 to act. Sainsbury's, Co-op and Albert Heijn followed in 2024-25. [Mercy For Animals](https://mercyforanimals.org/blog/tesco-shrimp-welfare-progress/)
- 2025-09: Les Mousquetaires published its shrimp commitment in a report. [Mousquetaires PDF](https://www.mousquetaires.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/09/250929-rapport-bbfaw-par-filiere.pdf)
- 2026 so far: roughly 6 of the 20 added commitments (Asda, Aldi, Auchan, Système U, Carrefour, Lidl). That is about 4-6 per year, driven mostly by campaigns in the UK and then France.
- Commitments are rarely retracted. I found no retraction by any of the listed retailers.
- The 9 remaining retailers are German, Iberian, Swiss, Russian, Metro, plus Leclerc. These markets have less NGO pressure on shrimp so far. Germany is the newest target.

## 5. Other forecasts
- I found no Polymarket, Kalshi or Manifold market on this question. None of the supplied market prices (DOJ beef suits, NYC grocery stores, Ryder Cup and others) is relevant.
- I could not find the community forecast on the Metaculus question.

## 6. Upcoming events before 2027-07-01
- ICAW's ongoing campaigns in Germany and Switzerland could produce commitments from Lidl Germany, Rewe, Edeka or Migros.
- Pressure on Leclerc is continuing after the ICAW report.
- SWP may update its resolution page to add the French retailers, Aldi and Lidl.
- Carrefour's 2027 stunning work and the ASC electrical-stunning trial that Lidl plans to join could firm up commitments that are currently partial.
- In the Netherlands, a 2024 Tweede Kamer motion asked the government to push supermarkets to stop selling ablated shrimp. [Hart van Nederland](https://www.hartvannederland.nl/politiek/artikelen/meerderheid-tweede-kamer-wil-verkoop-van-garnalen-met-afgeknipte-ogen)
- Risk of downward revision: whether resolvers count subsidiary or single-country policies (Albert Heijn, Lidl GB or France, Aldi Süd vs Aldi Nord) or ablation-only commitments such as Carrefour's.

forecasts.reasoning:
**(a) Time left:** About 8 months. Forecasts close on 2027-06-30 and the question resolves around 2027-07-01.

**(b) Latest known value:**
- The SWP page (last updated 2026-02-16) lists 6 of the 20 named retailers: Tesco, Sainsbury's, Co-op, Asda, Ahold Delhaize via Albert Heijn, and Intermarché via Les Mousquetaires.
- As of early November 2026, credible press reports cover about 13. The additional 7 are Auchan, Système U, Carrefour, Aldi, Schwarz/Lidl, Metro and Rewe.

**(c) If nothing changed:** About 13 on a liberal reading of "any commitment". The count would be about 11 or 12 if Rewe's "aim" or Metro's supplier "request" is excluded. It would be about 6 if the resolver relied strictly on the SWP page, which seems unlikely given the "credible sources" wording.

**(d) If the current trend continued:** About 7 retailers were added over the past 9 months. However, the easy targets in the UK, France and the German discounters are now done. The remaining retailers are:
- Leclerc, which has publicly refused.
- Edeka, which declined to comment.
- Migros, which is plausible given Swiss law already requires decapods to be stunned, and it may have an undiscovered statement.
- Mercadona, Jerónimo Martins, Magnit and X5, which are unlikely.

That suggests roughly 0 to 2 more, for a count of about 14.

**(e) Historical variation:** The count rose from about 1 in 2024 to about 6 in February 2026 and about 13 in November 2026. Over 8 months, a change of +0 to +3 is plausible. Retractions are rare.

**(f) Experts and markets:** No matching market or Metaculus forecast was found. The ICAW and SWP campaigns targeting Leclerc and German retailers are active.

**(g) Unexpected scenarios:**
- **Low:** The resolver relies mostly on the SWP list and strictly excludes vague or subsidiary-only pledges such as Metro, Rewe, Carrefour and the Lidl/Aldi group mapping. The count would end up around 7 to 9.
- **High:** Leclerc gives in to the ICAW campaign, Edeka follows Rewe and Lidl, and a Migros policy surfaces. The count would reach about 16, or 17 if one of the Iberian or Russian retailers also turns out to have a policy.
